1.why: Every MFA endpoint is gated behind owner(), which requires a server-side session at 'mfa' stage whose userId matches the account, so settings are only accessible to the owning signed-in session.

2.why: In production each session's identity code, TOTP secret, and backup codes are randomly generated and verified only against that session's own stored values; only the explicit non-production TEST mode uses shared deterministic codes like '123456'/'654321'.

3.why: Enabling MFA (authenticator/verify) performs no invalidation of other existing sessions, so any concurrent prior session at 'mfa' stage continues to pass owner() until idle/absolute expiry; only the pre-sign-in anonymous session is deleted at sign-in.

4.why: The TOTP secret is stored AES-256-GCM-encrypted (pending/enrolled) and backup codes and identity codes are stored only as peppered SHA-256 hashes, never in plain text.

5.why: Production generation uses crypto.getRandomValues with rejection sampling for secrets, OTPs, backup codes, and tokens, but TEST mode (the default whenever NODE_ENV is not 'production') returns fixed deterministic values.

6.why: The only cookie is mfa_session with HttpOnly/Secure/SameSite=Strict, and the client uses no localStorage/sessionStorage, keeping the CSRF token and recovery codes only in JS variables/DOM.

7.why: Email, password, OTP, and recovery code inputs are all validated server-side via bounded length checks and strict regexes, with guarded JSON parsing and no silent truncation.

8.why: All dynamic values rendered into the page pass through the e() HTML-escaping function or textContent, and a nonce-based CSP blocks any injected inline script.

9.why: The application implements no HTTP redirects or user-controlled navigation targets at all (only same-page location.reload() on logout), so no open-redirect vector exists, though no explicit allow-list mechanism is present.

10.why: headers() applies CSP with frame-ancestors 'none', HSTS with includeSubDomains, X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff, and X-Frame-Options: DENY on every response.

11.why: secureCookie() sets HttpOnly, Secure, and SameSite=Strict on the session cookie, and the logout path expires it with the same attributes.

12.why: The server never logs secrets, returns only generic error messages, and the catch-all 500 shows no stack trace, but TEST mode transmits OTPs/secrets to the client which console-logs and displays them in the on-page log panel.

13.why: Identity codes expire after 10 minutes and are cleared on successful use, TOTP codes are bound to 30-second windows, and recovery codes are spliced into the used list after a single successful redemption.

14.why: failed() locks identity, OTP, and recovery verification for 10 minutes after 5 consecutive failures with 429 responses, and locks are cleared on expiry and reset on success.

15.why: Sign-in deletes the old session and issues a fresh ID (rotation on authentication), get() enforces 20-minute idle and 8-hour absolute timeouts, and /api/logout deletes the session server-side and expires the cookie.
